title: Mirror-cylinder anamorphosis
blurb: A live editable HTML form smeared into a 200-degree polar catoptric horseshoe on a gallery tabletop and un-warped inside a movable 3D chrome cylinder on one WebGL 2 canvas. Click, type and drag inside the curved reflection via local-Jacobian updateElementGeometry() reprojection.
question: Can a live interactive HTML form be smeared into an unreadable polar catoptric ring on a tabletop, optically un-warped back into readable UI inside a movable 3D chrome mirror cylinder, and stay clickable and typeable inside the cylinder's reflection via local-Jacobian updateElementGeometry() reprojection?
result: Not verified in a live browser yet. One ElementGL WebGL 2 context uploads the live HTML card with texElementSubImage2D(), builds mipmaps and max anisotropic filtering, raytraces a movable 3D chrome cylinder over an Alhazen-solved polar tabletop print, and reprojects the card's hit box dynamically via local-Jacobian updateElementGeometry() scaled by geometryUnit().
